verdict: Sales jumped 13% to $6.26B as more shoppers came through the doors — sales at stores open a year rose 10% — and profit got an extra $253M boost from refunds of tariffs the government had collected.

takeaways.title: Shoppers drove the growth
takeaways.text: Comparable store sales rose 10%, mainly because more customers visited and bought, with both new and existing customers spending more.

takeaways.title: Profit up 67% — with a one-off tailwind
takeaways.text: Net income rose from $508M to $851M. About $253M of operating profit came from IEEPA tariff refunds; even without them, operating margin rose 205 basis points (2.05 percentage points).

takeaways.title: Outlook raised
takeaways.text: Ross raised full-year EPS guidance to $8.61–$8.77 and lifted its 2026 store-opening plan to 115 new stores after opening 47 in the quarter.

oneTimers: IEEPA tariff refunds of about $253M were recognized in the quarter, adding roughly $0.60 to EPS and about 405 basis points (4.05 percentage points) to operating margin.
footerNote: Q2 FY26 (13 weeks ended Aug 1, 2026) is used because Q3 FY26 — the quarter ending around Oct 31, 2026, due to be reported around Nov 19 — had not been reported as of Nov 7, 2026. Whole-$M rounding: tax is shown as $284M (reported $283M) so the rounded figures balance exactly. Segment split confirmed from the Q2 FY26 Form 10-Q: Ross has one reportable segment.
